$comment: Advisories consciously accepted, with an expiry date that forces re-review.
This is NOT a way to silence the audit gate: scripts/audit-gate.mjs fails the
build for any advisory that is not listed here, and ALSO fails for any entry
whose reviewBy date has passed. Adding an entry requires a real applicability

allow.package: picomatch (via vite, tinyglobby, fdir and @rollup/pluginutils; and via tailwindcss 3 -> chokidar, micromatch, anymatch, readdirp)
allow.title: picomatch vulnerable to ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs
justification: NOT REACHABLE IN THIS APPLICATION. The attack needs an attacker to choose the glob: a
pattern such as +(*) or +(*a) makes picomatch's regular expression backtrack
exponentially. Here picomatch runs only at build and test time, never in the app or in
api/. All four copies in package-lock.json (4.0.7, and 2.3.2 under anymatch, micromatch
and readdirp) are dev-only: `npm ls picomatch --omit=dev` is empty and
`npm audit --omit=dev` reports 0 advisories. The patterns it is given are written in
this repository and contain no extglob: the two Tailwind content globs in
tailwind.config.js, the vite-plugin-pwa globPatterns in vite.config.ts, the include
lists in vitest.config.ts and the ESLint ignores. No app code or script imports
picomatch, micromatch, anymatch, readdirp, tinyglobby or fdir, and none of them is in
the built bundle (Tailwind ships static CSS), so no user input ever reaches them. The
Vite dev server and CI only run on a developer's machine or in GitHub Actions, against
this repository's own files.
NO FORWARD FIX EXISTS. The advisory covers picomatch <=4.0.7. GitHub lists no patched
version and 4.0.7 is the latest release (npm dist-tag latest; `npm view
"picomatch@>4.0.7"` finds nothing; checked 2026-11-18), so no lockfile update can
reach a patched copy. The 2.x line ends at 2.3.2, also in range, and the 2.x copies are
pinned inside Tailwind 3: tailwindcss 3.4.19 (the last 3.x) needs chokidar ^3.6.0, whose
last release needs readdirp ~3.6.0 and anymatch ~3.1.2, and fast-glob ^3.3.2, which
needs micromatch ^4.0.8 (picomatch ^2.3.1). An npm override would only move them to
another vulnerable release. npm's remediation is tailwindcss 4, a semver-major
migration of the whole design system, which is a project of its own.
ACTION ON EXPIRY: check for a picomatch release above 4.0.7 and run `npm update
picomatch --package-lock-only`; for the 2.x copies, check for micromatch, anymatch and
readdirp releases that drop 2.x, or plan the Tailwind 4 migration. Delete this entry as
soon as a patched version is installed (the gate also flags it as stale). If anything
ever passes user-supplied globs or patterns to these packages, delete this entry
immediately: the argument above no longer holds.
